messages.text: Defensive 'masterclass' and elite Rice - how Arsenal ended Anfield torment

metadata.summary: Not since 2012 - when current boss Mikel Arteta was commanding Arsenal's midfield on the pitch - had the Gunners won on Liverpool’s patch. That curse has finally been broken.
metadata.content: Arsenal's 'defensive masterclass' praised in Liverpool win as Jamie Carragher salutes 'world class' Declan Rice | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Arsenal's 'defensive masterclass' praised in Liverpool win as Jamie Carragher salutes 'world class' Declan Rice Arsenal eked out a first victory at Anfield for 14 years by beating Liverpool 1-0 thanks to Kai Havertz’s first-half winner; Jamie Carragher called their defensive performance outstanding and reserved special praise for Declan Rice Laura Hunter Football Features Writer Sunday 1 November 2026 23:29, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Daniel Sturridge heaps praise on Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta for what he's built with the Gunners and says his system is 'almost perfect'. Not since 2012 - when current boss Mikel Arteta was commanding Arsenal's midfield on the pitch - had the Gunners won on Liverpool’s patch. That curse has finally been broken. Winning at Anfield is a rarity, especially for Arsenal. But Arteta's side were ruthless at both ends of the pitch, a tactical triumph for the boss and one that underlines his side's champion mentality. "I love when there is something that we haven't done for many years," beamed the Spaniard, who praised his players for a defensive performance he called "remarkable". If Arteta wanted to make a statement, he succeeded. Liverpool 0-1 Arsenal - Report and highlights Live Premier League table | Watch FREE PL highlights Got Sky? Watch Premier League

messages.text: Antonelli crowned world champion as Verstappen wins wild Mexico City GP

metadata.summary: Kimi Antonelli became the youngest Formula 1 world champion in history as Max Verstappen held off Lewis Hamilton to win a thrilling Mexico City Grand Prix.
metadata.content: Kimi Antonelli crowned 2026 F1 world champion as Max Verstappen wins wild Mexico City Grand Prix from Lewis Hamilton | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Kimi Antonelli crowned 2026 F1 world champion as Max Verstappen wins wild Mexico City Grand Prix from Lewis Hamilton Kimi Antonelli has won the 2026 F1 Drivers' Championship at 20 years and 68 days old, breaking Sebastian Vettel's record for youngest world champion by three years; Max Verstappen won a wild Mexico City Grand Prix from Lewis Hamilton amid drama between the Ferrari drivers Nigel Chiu Sports Journalist @NigelCJourno Sunday 1 November 2026 23:24, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix as Kimi Antonelli became the youngest world champion in F1 history Kimi Antonelli became the youngest Formula 1 world champion in history as Max Verstappen held off Lewis Hamilton to win a thrilling Mexico City Grand Prix. Antonelli finished third to secure the F1 Drivers' Championship with four rounds to spare, becoming the first Italian world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953. The 20-year-old avoided all the chaos in one of the most action-packed races of the season and was hugely emotional after the chequered flag. messages.text: Sale secures Grand Final title and Brown crowned Road to Mallorca No 1

metadata.summary: Julien Sale produced a dominant final round to secure victory at the HotelPlanner Tour’s Grand Final, while Hamish Brown topped the Road to Mallorca rankings.
metadata.content: HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final: Julien Sale secures title, Hamish Brown crowned Road to Mallorca No 1 and DP World Tour cards confirmed | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final: Julien Sale secures title, Hamish Brown crowned Road to Mallorca No 1 and DP World Tour cards confirmed HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final sees France's Julien Sale claim title and Denmark's Hamish Brown finish top of the Road to Mallorca Rankings; Sale ends year second in rankings and will now step up to golf's DP World Tour for the first time in his career Sunday 1 November 2026 19:06, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day four of the HotelPlanner Tour Grand Final at the Club de Golf Alcanada in Mallorca, Spain Julien Sale produced a dominant final round to secure victory at the HotelPlanner Tour’s Grand Final, while Hamish Brown topped the Road to Mallorca rankings. Frenchman Sale, who was guaranteed promotion to the DP World Tour before the season finale in Mallorca, posted his second 65 of the week to reach 22 under par, four strokes clear of the Brown, who narrowly held onto solo second to capture the season-long title. Sale ends the year second in the rankings and will now step up to golf's DP World Tour for the first time in his career.
